Content:
We wish to prove that

Content:
[MATH: S_{xx} = ∑_(i)x_{i}^{2} − (1)/(n)(∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i})^{2}.]

Content:
We start with the definition of [MATH: S_{xx}{:}]

Content:
[MATH: S_{xx}|= ∑_(i = 1)^(n)(x_{i} − x^(―))^{2}]

Content:
First, we expand the binomial:

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(n)(x_{i}^{2} − 2x_{i} ⋅ x^(―) + x^(―)^{2})]

Content:
Distributing the summation, we have

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − ∑_(i = 1)^(n)2x_{i} ⋅ x^(―) + ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x^(―)^{2}.]

Content:
Now, since [MATH: 2, \overline x,] and [MATH: \overline{x}^2] are constants, we can write this as

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − 2x^(―) ⋅ ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i} + x^(―)^{2} ⋅ ∑_(i = 1)^(n)1.]

Content:
Next, we use the following results:

Content:
[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^n x_i = n\overline x, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^n 1 = n]

Content:
This gives

Content:
[MATH: S_{xx}|= ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − 2x^(―) ⋅ nx^(―) + x^(―)^{2} ⋅ n; = ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − 2nx^(―)^{2} + nx^(―)^{2}; = ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − nx^(―)^{2}; = ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − n ⋅ ((1)/(n)∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i})^{2}; = ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − n ⋅ (1)/(n^{2}) ⋅ (∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i})^{2}; = ∑_(i)x_{i}^{2} − (1)/(n)(∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i})^{2}]
as required.

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Given a data set [MATH: x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n,] we know that its variance, which we may denote as [MATH: \sigma_x^2,] is given by

Content:
[MATH: \sigma_x^2 = \dfrac1n \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline x)^2]
where [MATH: \overline x] is the mean of [MATH: x.]

Content:
The summation term

Content:
[MATH: S_{xx} = \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline x)^2]
is known as a sum of squares and is denoted [MATH: S_{xx}.] As we'll see, this quantity often appears in statistical analysis, so giving it a separate notation is useful.

Content:
Similarly, if we have a data set [MATH: y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n,] then we define
[MATH: S_{yy} = \sum_{i=1}^n (y_i - \overline y)^2.]

Content:
Now, suppose we have the bivariate data set
[MATH: (x_1, y_1), \qquad (x_2, y_2),\qquad \ldots, \qquad (x_n, y_n).]
Then, the covariance is given by
[MATH: \textrm{Cov}(x,y) = \dfrac1n\sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline x)(y_i - \overline y)]
and we may define [MATH: S_{xy}] as
[MATH: S_{xy} = \sum_{i=1}^n (x_i - \overline{x})(y_i - \overline{y}).]

Content:
Finally, we can define the variance and covariance in terms of [MATH: S_{xx}, S_{yy},] and [MATH: S_{xy}] as follows:
[MATH: σ_{x}^{2}|= (S_{xx})/(n), σ_{y}^{2} = (S_{yy})/(n), Cov(x, y) = (S_{xy})/(n)]

[MATH: S_{xy}|= ∑_(i = 1)^(n)(x_{i} − x^(―))(y_{i} − y^(―)).]

First, we calculate the sample means [MATH: \overline{x}] and [MATH: \overline{y}{:}]

Next, we calculate the differences between the [MATH: x_i] and [MATH: \overline{x}], [MATH: y_i] and [MATH: \overline{y}], and their product.

Item 15 — Tutorial: Proving the Shortcut Formulas

Content:
We wish to prove that

Content:
[MATH: S_{xx} = ∑_(i)x_{i}^{2} − (1)/(n)(∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i})^{2}.]

Content:
We start with the definition of [MATH: S_{xx}{:}]

Content:
[MATH: S_{xx}|= ∑_(i = 1)^(n)(x_{i} − x^(―))^{2}]

Content:
First, we expand the binomial:

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(n)(x_{i}^{2} − 2x_{i} ⋅ x^(―) + x^(―)^{2})]

Content:
Distributing the summation, we have

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − ∑_(i = 1)^(n)2x_{i} ⋅ x^(―) + ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x^(―)^{2}.]

Content:
Now, since [MATH: 2, \overline x,] and [MATH: \overline{x}^2] are constants, we can write this as

Content:
[MATH: ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − 2x^(―) ⋅ ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i} + x^(―)^{2} ⋅ ∑_(i = 1)^(n)1.]

Content:
Next, we use the following results:

Content:
[MATH: \sum_{i=1}^n x_i = n\overline x, \qquad \sum_{i=1}^n 1 = n]

Content:
This gives

Content:
[MATH: S_{xx}|= ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − 2x^(―) ⋅ nx^(―) + x^(―)^{2} ⋅ n; = ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − 2nx^(―)^{2} + nx^(―)^{2}; = ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − nx^(―)^{2}; = ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − n ⋅ ((1)/(n)∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i})^{2}; = ∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i}^{2} − n ⋅ (1)/(n^{2}) ⋅ (∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i})^{2}; = ∑_(i)x_{i}^{2} − (1)/(n)(∑_(i = 1)^(n)x_{i})^{2}]
as required.
